Grey-brown spots with straight edges, limited by the leaf veins, so they look angular. Spots can join, and leaves may yellow and fall early. Pods can show reddish-brown spots.
Through infected seed, crop leftovers in the soil, and rain splash or wind.

string-array.name: angular_leaf_spot_do_now
string-array.item: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves and plants. Do not leave them in the field.
Avoid working in the field when plants are wet.
If the disease is spreading, ask your extension officer which fungicide is approved locally.

string-array.name: angular_leaf_spot_prevent
string-array.item: Rotate with a non-bean crop for at least 2 seasons.
Plough under or remove crop leftovers after harvest.

resources.string: Small, raised, rusty-brown powdery spots, mostly on the underside of leaves, often with a yellow ring. Rubbing a spot leaves brown powder on your finger.
Spores carried by wind. Humid weather and morning dew help it spread.

string-array.name: bean_rust_do_now
string-array.item: Do not work among wet plants. You will spread the spores.
If the disease is spreading, ask your extension officer which fungicide is approved locally.

string-array.name: bean_rust_prevent
string-array.item: Give plants enough space for air to move.
Remove volunteer bean plants and crop leftovers.

resources.string: No disease signs found on this leaf.

string-array.name: healthy_keep_healthy
string-array.item: Check your plants every week, especially after rain.
Scan several leaves from different parts of the field. One healthy leaf does not mean the whole field is healthy.
Keep using clean seed and crop rotation.

resources.string: How to take a good photo
Fill the frame with a single leaf.
Avoid harsh direct sun and strong shadows.
Keep the phone still and tap the leaf on the screen to focus.
Photograph the top side of the leaf, where the spots are easiest to see.
